record.paper_title: Modeling social resilience: Questions, answers, open problems
record.original_question: How should time-window size, event-time thresholds, and temporal paths be chosen when reconstructing interaction networks from temporal observations? The question matters because these choices determine network density, topological analyses, and who can potentially influence whom in a social organization.

evidence.quote: Choosing the right window size is a problem in itself, because the window size impacts the network density and subsequently all topological analyses.
Only observations with a ∆t lower than a given threshold ∆tthr will count as interactions
The problem, who can potentially inﬂuence whom, requires to reconstruct temporal paths of various lengths

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{O} = \{(i_k, j_k, t_k)\}_{k=1}^N$ be a finite sequence of timestamped pairwise observations among a set $V$ of agents, where $(i_k, j_k, t_k)$ records an observed interaction between $i_k, j_k \in V$ at time $t_k \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$. From $\mathcal{O}$ one reconstructs an interaction network in three customary ways:

1. (Window aggregation.) Given a window size $w > 0$ and an offset $s \ge 0$, form the static graph $G_{w,s} = (V, E_{w,s})$ in which $\{i,j\} \in E_{w,s}$ iff there exists at least one observation $(i,j,t) \in \mathcal{O}$ with $t \in [s, s+w]$. The edge density and all derived topological statistics (degree distribution, clustering, components, centralities) depend on $w$ and $s$.

2. (Event-time thresholding.) Given two consecutive observations involving the same pair, only those whose inter-event gap $\Delta t$ satisfies $\Delta t \le \Delta t_{\mathrm{thr}}$ are counted as a sustained interaction edge; the resulting edge set depends on the threshold $\Delta t_{\mathrm{thr}} > 0$.

3. (Temporal paths.) A temporal path of length $\ell$ from $u$ to $v$ is a sequence $(u = v_0, v_1, \dots, v_\ell = v)$ together with times $t_1 < t_2 < \cdots < t_\ell$ such that each $(v_{r-1}, v_r, t_r)$ is an observation. Reachability "who can potentially influence whom" is encoded by the set $R_{\ell,\tau}(u) = \{v : \exists \text{ temporal path of length } \le \ell \text{ from } u \text{ to } v \text{ with } t_\ell - t_1 \le \tau\}$.

Problem. Provide principled, data-driven rules for choosing the parameters $w$, $s$, $\Delta t_{\mathrm{thr}}$, $\ell$, and $\tau$ from $\mathcal{O}$ so that the reconstructed networks $G_{w,s}$ and the temporal reachability sets $R_{\ell,\tau}(\cdot)$ faithfully represent the underlying interaction structure. In particular: (a) determine an optimal window size $w^*$ that balances statistical stability of topological observables against temporal resolution; (b) determine an optimal inter-event threshold $\Delta t_{\mathrm{thr}}^*$ separating genuine interactions from spurious co-occurrences; (c) determine path-length and time-horizon parameters $\ell^*, \tau^*$ for meaningful potential-influence reachability. Prove or characterize the existence, uniqueness, and consistency of such optima under a stated stochastic model of the observation process.
artifact.status_search_result: The choice of time-window size, inter-event thresholds, and temporal-path parameters in reconstructing interaction networks from temporal data remains an active methodological research question with no universally accepted optimal procedure; multiple heuristics (e.g., natural-timescale, activity-driven, motif-based) have been proposed, but no canonical solution has been established.
